messages:
ana: heads up — after upgrading our dev image to the rpm build of redwoodctl on RHEL 9, my systemd --user unit for local-serve can't read the token. it works when i run it in my shell but service logs show: avc:  denied  { read } for  pid=12345 comm=\"redwoodctl\" name=\"token\" dev=\"sda1\" ino=56789 scontext=system_u:system_r:container_t:s0 tcontext=user_u:object_r:user_home_t:s0 tclass=file
jordan: that avc looks like selinux denying container_t -> user_home_t access. weird that running in shell is fine (shell runs in unconfined_t?), systemd user unit might be labeled container_t by our packaging script.
lee: packaging? the rpm's /usr/bin/redwoodctl has a systemd unit file in /usr/lib/systemd/user/redwood-local-serve.service right? any ExecStart= wrapper?
nana: (typo: i'm ana not nana)
nana: fwiw the rpm installs a small helper that drops you into a sandbox'd mode via systemd TemporaryFileSystem and uses `systemd-run --scope -p Type=simple` to isolate. maybe SELinux context is injected there.
maria: quick checks: `ps -eZ | grep redwoodctl` when run as service vs shell to compare scontext.
nana: service shows: system_u:system_r:container_t:s0 and shell run shows unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0. so service is container_t and can't access user_home_t by policy.
jordan: temporary workaround: `chcon -t container_file_t ~/.config/redwood/token` makes it readable to container_t but that's not great for customers. We need package fix or selinux policy tweak.
nana: another workaround: set `PrivateTmp=no`/remove sandboxing in the unit for user installs, but that reduces isolation for the service. Not great for shared dev boxes.
nana: suggestion: rpm postinstall should not ship a systemd unit that wraps `redwoodctl local-serve` into a container_t context for user services. For system-wide deploys we can provide a system unit that runs under system_t and is documented.
lee: agree. also add a `redwoodctl doctor --selinux` check that warns when service context != unconfined_t and suggests `chcon --recursive -t container_file_t ~/.config/redwood` or revert packaging unit.
maria: filing a policy issue is fine, but we shouldn't recommend chcon to customers by default. Maybe better: package ships a small selinux module `redwoodctl_local_serve.pp` that allows container_t read access to %user_home_dir%/.config/redwood(token). Installer can prompt to install it for enterprise images.
jordan: for now I'll update the rpm to not enable the user unit by default. That avoids surprise for users. Add note in upgrade changelog.
dev-bot: created issue DX-1499: "rpm package: systemd user unit runs redwoodctl under container_t causing SELinux denials reading ~/.config/redwood token" assigned to @jordan P2.
nana: thanks — i'll add repro steps and logs to the issue and test the disable-by-default fix.
nana: also adding `redwoodctl docs install` note for RHEL users about `restorecon -Rv ~/.config/redwood` if they want to keep the unit enabled.
maria: ok nice. :white_check_mark:
